text: {"score":4,"justification":"Numbers match the card and tool outputs. The 10,447 and 16,450 figures come from the final estimate_overpayment output (24 of 30 reviewed), so they are grounded. The headline, 5 of 24 below billed, matches the final hybrid_review. Documentation stats (4 documented 99215, 3 below, 75%; 1 of 9 data-without-test) match the card. The summary flags that 6 charts are missing, notes the estimate is less certain, and gives concrete next steps. Weaknesses: the 'excess shows up in every complexity group' claim is loosely supported, since the 0-complexity group is 7.1% against an all-provider 2% but the card gives no expected figure per group. The text repeats the 18.2% vs 4.4% statement. It never says explicitly that it is a reason to review and not a finding, unlike the draft_summary. Cited claim C0085576, C0085628 and C0085650 have no documentation, so they support only the low-complexity point. The 'against 3% for comparison providers' wording is roughly right (the card's all_provider_rate is 7.7% for 99215, while the tool says 3%), so this is a mild inconsistency with the card.","problems":["'Excess shows up in every complexity group' is not clearly supported; the card gives no per-group expected shares, only the provider's share against the all-provider share.","Redundant sentence repeating 18.2% vs 4.4%.","The comparison rate of 3% for 99215 below-billed conflicts with the card's all_provider_rate of 0.077 for 99215 (the 3% appears to come from tool output or the all-level rate).","Lacks the explicit 'reason to review, not a finding' caution found in the draft output; the caution relies on the leaning label and the coder-review note.","Three of the six cited claims have no documentation and serve only as low-complexity examples; the 'CI' is wide and the summary does not highlight that."]}
